classification.difficultyReason: Rearranges the sector-area formula to find a radius and an angle, retaining exact values.

content.prompt: Let the sector subtended by angle $\theta$ have area $625\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

spec.description: Unshaded downward-opening narrow sector with its centre at the top, a curved lower boundary, two radii labelled r with matching single ticks, and an internal angle arc labelled theta. The drawn angle is schematic, not a numerical given.
spec.mathematics: Both straight boundaries are equal radii r; their included central angle is theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent shared givens only; no calculated answers.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $\theta$ if $r=8\text{ cm}$.

answer.short: No ordinary sector satisfies these givens; formal substitution gives $\theta=\dfrac{625\pi}{32}$ radians.
answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12r^2\theta\\625\pi&=\frac12\times8^2\times\theta\\625\pi&=32\theta\\\theta&=\frac{625\pi}{32}\text{ radians}\end{aligned}$

This exceeds $2\pi$ radians. A circle of radius $8\text{ cm}$ has area $64\pi\text{ cm}^2$, so it cannot contain a sector of area $625\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
